body:
Arming auto-merge marks a PR as handled for every downstream repair path, so an
armed PR that *cannot* merge becomes permanently invisible instead of merely slow.

The three paths and why each declines it:

- GitHub itself will not merge an armed PR whose `mergeable` is `CONFLICTING`.
- `scripts/finish-armed-automerges.sh:188` skips `mergeable != MERGEABLE`
  ("conflicts or unknown"). This is correct in isolation — it completes merges,
  it does not resolve conflicts — but it is the only thing that acts on armed PRs.
- `scripts/report-orphaned-prs.sh:213` selects only PRs with a non-null
  `autoMergeRequest` into the STUCK-ARMED bucket, and the ORPHAN bucket at :283
  selects the complement. So an armed PR can never be reported as an orphan, and
  the orphan rule is what tells phase-7 it must finish something.

The net effect is a PR that reports itself every tick and is repaired by nobody.
The STUCK-ARMED bucket was added after #1324 hit this on 2026-08-03, and the
comment at report-orphaned-prs.sh:192-202 documents the seam — but it added
*detection only*, so the row now recurs instead of the PR landing.

MEASURED on state/completed.log: `tick-stuck-armed-prs` has fired 11 times across
two PRs. #1324 on 2026-08-08 through 2026-08-10 (7 rows), then #1580 on
2026-08-13, armed by github-actions at 02:34:32Z and still CONFLICTING 8h19m
later. #1580 was tier-1 and CHANGELOG-only; the conflict was an ordinary
`[Unreleased]` union that resolves mechanically.

Repaired by hand this tick (#1580 -> f3fdb1345, DIRTY -> MERGEABLE), which fixes
the instance and not the mechanism.

Worth noting the conflict class is highly predictable: every merged PR appends to
CHANGELOG.md `[Unreleased]`, so two PRs touching it conflict by construction.
That is already recorded as a recurring cost in project memory
(needs-review-pile-rots-into-changelog-conflicts, 2026-07-18, when all four pile
PRs were CONFLICTING at once).

Two candidate fixes, smallest first:

1. Stop exempting a *non-mergeable* armed PR from the orphan rule. For those the
   arm is provably not working, so the exemption's premise ("the finisher will
   get it") is false. One predicate change; turns an invisible PR into reported
   work phase-7 must finish.
2. Teach the finisher to un-rot a tier-1 CHANGELOG-only conflict by union. Higher
   value and higher risk — an automated resolver that gets it wrong corrupts
   release notes, so it needs red/green tests over real conflict shapes, and it
   must drop entries main has since moved into a released section rather than
   reinstating them.

Related: F-1760ca (withdrawing merge authorisation does not disable auto-merge)
is the same subsystem and the adjacent half of the arming lifecycle.
title: An armed auto-merge that cannot merge is exempted by every repair path
